caption: Hebrews directly applies God’s father-son promise to Jesus. That is strong Christian evidence—but in Samuel, royal sonship first describes Solomon and David’s dynasty.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did God promise His Son to David? God says David’s heir will be His son. Luke and Romans apply Davidic sonship language to Jesus.
slides.body: God says David’s heir will be His son. Luke and Romans apply Davidic sonship language to Jesus.
slides.heading: Did God promise His Son to David?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of 2Sam 7:14a: I will be his Father, and he will be My son.
slides.body: I will be his Father, and he will be My son.
slides.heading: 2Sam 7:14a

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Heb 1:5, BSB: For to which of the angels did God ever say: ‘I will be His Father, and He will be My Son’?
slides.body: For to which of the angels did God ever say: ‘I will be His Father, and He will be My Son’?
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Heb 1:5

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Hebrews makes the link explicit Hebrews directly quotes this line about Jesus. The Christian application is part of the New Testament itself.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the first son is Solomon The full verse allows for wrongdoing and discipline. This is royal sonship for David’s heir, not yet a claim that the king is God.
